extra.message: Hardcoded/weak JWT secret key allows token forgery — Attacker can mint valid JWTs for any user (including admin) without credentials, achieving full authentication bypass [verified: app.py:15 hardcodes JWT_SECRET_KEY as the static, well-known string 'dvga' used by flask_graphql_auth to sign tokens; anyone can forge valid JWTs for any identity, achieving full authentication bypass.]

Flask debug mode enabled by default — Remote code execution via Werkzeug interactive debugger and disclosure of source code/environment in stack traces [verified: config.py:11 defaults WEB_DEBUG to True unless explicitly overridden, and this is a known intentionally-vulnerable app so the insecure default is genuinely present on a reachable path. This enables the Werkzeug interactive debugger, allowing RCE and source/stack-trace disclosure.]

JWT signature verification disabled in get_identity — Attacker can forge a JWT with any identity claim (e.g. 'admin') to access resolve_me and any code path relying on get_identity, since the signature is never verified [verified: Duplicate/combined finding of unverified JWT decode (helpers.py:21); plaintext password comparison is separate but also unmitigated, both confirming broken authentication.]

Path traversal in UploadPaste file write — Arbitrary file write/overwrite anywhere the app process can write, potentially leading to RCE (e.g. overwriting app code or cron files) [verified: Duplicate of finding 0 - same unsanitized WEB_UPLOADDIR + filename concatenation in save_file.]

Spoofable 'identity' field in request JSON bypasses admin check to leak plaintext passwords — Unauthenticated attacker dumps plaintext passwords for all users via a crafted request body field, leading to full account takeover. [verified: Same root cause as idx 6 — identity is read from the attacker-controlled JSON body, not any verified session state.]

Client-supplied identity field in request body bypasses password field authorization — Any unauthenticated attacker can dump all users' passwords via a crafted GraphQL request body. [verified: resolve_password checks info.context.json.get('identity')=='admin', where context.json is the raw attacker-supplied request body, not a verified token/session.]

Missing authorization / IDOR on paste and admin mutations — Any user (including unauthenticated ones, since no @mutation_jwt_required-style decorator is applied here) can edit or delete any other user's pastes, dump all users/audits, or wipe the entire paste table [verified: All listed resolvers/mutations lack any authentication/authorization/ownership check in views.py, consistent with the DVGA threat model gap on admin/paste resolvers.]

OS command injection via ImportPaste host/path/scheme (also SSRF) — Arbitrary command execution on the server; also enables SSRF to internal network resources [verified: strip_dangerous_characters denylist only strips ';' and '&', leaving backticks/$()/pipes usable in path/host to inject commands into the curl string passed to os.popen.]

SSRF and shell injection via ImportPaste host/path/scheme — Server-side request forgery against internal network/cloud metadata endpoints, and potential command execution via unfiltered shell metacharacters [verified: strip_dangerous_characters only removes ';' and '&'; backticks/$()/pipes reach os.popen via run_cmd, and host/port/scheme are fully attacker-controlled enabling SSRF too.]

OS command injection via system_diagnostics cmd argument — Authenticated (or default-easy-mode) attacker executes arbitrary shell commands on the server host [verified: In easy mode allowed_cmds always returns True, and even hard mode's startswith check is bypassable with trailing shell metacharacters before hitting run_cmd->os.popen.]

Missing authorization on delete_all_pastes and admin-data queries — Any unauthenticated user can wipe all paste data or dump full user/audit records [verified: resolve_delete_all_pastes, resolve_users, resolve_audits have zero auth/authz checks in the file — no decorator or identity check gates them.]

IDOR on EditPaste/DeletePaste by paste id — Any user can modify or delete pastes belonging to other users without ownership verification [verified: EditPaste/DeletePaste operate via Paste.query.filter_by(id=id) with no ownership/session check tying id to requester.]

Missing authorization on deletePaste mutation — Any client can delete arbitrary pastes belonging to other users. [verified: DeletePaste.mutate deletes by id with no ownership or authentication check, confirmed at views.py:164-169.]

SQL injection via pastes filter argument — Attacker can read/modify arbitrary database contents or bypass query logic via crafted filter value containing SQL syntax [verified: Confirmed same SQLi as idx 3; text() built via % string formatting of raw filter with no escaping.]

Unauthenticated search exposes private pastes and all users — Anonymous attacker can enumerate all usernames and read the content/title of private pastes belonging to other users via the search query, bypassing the public/private access control enforced elsewhere. [verified: resolve_search (views.py:298-312) queries Paste and User with no auth check, no public filter, and no Audit-based access gate, unlike resolve_pastes which defaults public=False; any anonymous caller enumerates usernames and reads private pastes by keyword.]

SQL injection via pastes filter argument — Attacker can manipulate the WHERE clause to bypass the public/burn filters, extract private paste data, or perform blind SQLi to exfiltrate the database [verified: resolve_pastes (views.py:314-322) builds text("title='%s' or content='%s'" % (filter, filter)) via raw string formatting with no binding/escaping.]

Plaintext password storage — Any DB read access, backup leak, or SQL injection (already present in resolve_pastes) exposes all user passwords in cleartext, enabling full account takeover and credential-stuffing against reused passwords elsewhere. [verified: Confirmed: models.py:14 stores password as plain String, CreateUser stores raw password, Login compares plaintext, and no hashing library is used anywhere in the codebase.]

Stored XSS via unsanitized paste title/content — Stored script execution in the context of any user viewing the paste (session/token theft, CSRF-token exfiltration) [verified: CreatePaste/EditPaste store title/content verbatim with no sanitization and PasteObject exposes raw fields for rendering with no escaping shown in this file.]

Missing authorization on read_and_burn query — Attacker can read and permanently destroy any burn-paste by guessing/enumerating IDs, denying legitimate recipients access. [verified: resolve_read_and_burn fetches and deletes by id with no auth/ownership check, enabling enumeration and destruction of others' burn pastes.]

GraphiQL access control bypass via unsigned client cookie — Attacker can trivially enable GraphiQL (introspection/debug UI) by setting a plain unsigned cookie, exposing the full schema and query console even when the app intends to disable it at higher difficulty settings [verified: IGQLProtectionMiddleware.resolve at middleware.py:122-126 gates GraphiQL solely on a plain unsigned 'env' cookie set via resp.set_cookie (views.py:395), not a signed session; any client can set this cookie to bypass the gate and enable introspection/GraphiQL UI at medium difficulty. Impact is limited (only affects GraphiQL/introspection exposure, not auth/data) so severity is low, but the control ]

GraphQL batching enabled with no query cost/depth limiting enables resource-exhaustion DoS — Attacker can amplify load via batched/aliased unbounded queries causing resource exhaustion [verified: resolve_search with no keyword returns unbounded Paste/User query.all(), and resolve_pastes defaults limit=1000; CostProtection only weights systemUpdate at cost 10, leaving these paths effectively unmetered under batching.]

Insecure cookie flags on GraphiQL access-control cookie — Missing HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite lets the cookie be read/set via XSS or network interception, and its unsigned plaintext value lets any client trivially flip it to 'graphiql:enable' to bypass the access-control middleware. [verified: views.py:395 sets the 'env' cookie with no HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite and no signature, and IGQLProtectionMiddleware trusts its raw value, so a client can trivially set env=graphiql:enable to bypass the gate; low severity since GraphiQL exposure is a minor info-disclosure/DX control, not a direct data breach.]
